title: Car, Relax, Alone, Forget, Friends, Trouble (CRAFFT) Questionnaire
abbreviations: The Car, Relax, Alone, Forget, Friends/Family, Trouble (CRAFFT) Questionnaire
The Car, Relax, Alone, Forget, Friends, Trouble (CRAFFT) Questionnaire
formula:
**Part A**

Please ask your patient the following questions: During the past 12 months, how many days did you...

- Drink more than a few sips of beer, wine, or any drink containing alcohol?
- Use any marijuana (cannabis, weed, oil, wax, or hash, by smoking, vaping, dabbing, or in edibles) or “synthetic marijuana” (like “K2,” “Spice”)?
- Use anything else to get high (like other illegal drugs, pills, prescription or over-the-counter medications, and things that you sniff, huff, vape, or inject)?

**Part B**

If the patient answers “0” for all questions in Part A, please ask the CAR question only, then stop. Otherwise, please ask all six CRAFFT questions below:

| Question | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Have you ever ridden in a CAR driven by someone (including yourself) who was “high” or had been using alcohol or drugs? | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| Do you ever use alcohol or drugs to RELAX , feel better about yourself, or fit in? | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| Do you ever use alcohol or drugs while you are by yourself, ALONE ? | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| Do you ever FORGET things you did while using alcohol or drugs? | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| Do your family or FRIENDS ever tell you that you should cut down on your drinking or drug use? | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |
| Have you ever gotten into TROUBLE while you were using alcohol or drugs? | No | 0 |
| Yes | 1 | |

how_to_use.why:
- Designed to be brief and easy-to-use in the primary care setting.
- Simultaneously screens for alcohol and drug use.
- Enables clinicians to identify adolescents who may benefit from additional counseling and intervention for substance use.
- Suggested by the American Academy of Pediatrics’ Bright Futures toolkit.
how_to_use.when:
- Peut être utilisé pour dépister la consommation de substances chez les adolescents en soins primaires.
- Plusieurs groupes médicaux recommandent de dépister la consommation de substances chez tous les adolescents lors des consultations de santé de routine.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Dérivé de questions spécifiques des outils RAFFT, DAP et POSIT qui ont été identifiées comme sensibles, spécifiques et/ou cliniquement pertinentes dans des études de validation antérieures.
- Démontre une bonne sensibilité et spécificité pour identifier un usage problématique, un abus ou une dépendance.
- Peut être administré par un clinicien ou auto-administré.
- N'est pas destiné à servir d'outil diagnostique.

next_steps.advice:
- Adolescents who screen positive (score ≥ 2) should undergo further evaluation to formally diagnose a substance use disorder.
- Additional questions and discussions should follow any “yes” answer. This will guide management plans, counseling, and support measures.
- The “CAR” question is considered especially important, as young patients are at risk even if they do not use alcohol or drugs themselves. This warrants further information gathering, advice, action plans, and follow-up.
- ”Red flag” behaviors (e.g., using substances alone, episodes of amnesia due to substance use) may necessitate a referral to a treatment specialist.
- For more guidance, refer to the American Academy of Pediatrics’[clinical report](https://publications.aap.org/pediatrics/article/138/1/e20161211/52568/Substance-Use-Screening-Brief-Intervention-and?autologincheck=redirected?nfToken=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000).
